I'll write `bump.sh` that reads version.json, bumps the patch, writes it back, and creates tag.txt.

<tool_call>
<function=write>
<parameter=path>
bump.sh
</parameter>
<parameter=content>
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Read current version from version.json
MAJOR=$(python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('version.json'))['major'])")
MINOR=$(python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('version.json'))['minor'])")
PATCH=$(python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('version.json'))['patch'])")

# Bump patch
PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))

# Write version back
python3 -c "import json;json.dump({'major':${MAJOR},'minor':${MINOR},'patch':${PATCH}},open('version.json','w'))"

# Write tag.txt
echo "v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}" > tag.txt

</parameter>
</function>
